_note: ARM-2 S2 and ARM-3 P3: carrier advisories that put a corridor on another route (the same port pair by Suez or by the Cape of Good Hope). transit_delta_days and distance_delta_nm are written only where a stored notice states one figure verbatim, and each row's `absent` says per column why it is empty; fuel_burn_multiplier is never typed. The 2026-09-14 Maersk row cites its own notice (capture 17ad7849), so a later apply patches the source of row 92d35ddc from the 2023-12-15 article to it.

rows.cause: Maersk paused all vessels bound for the Red Sea / Gulf of Aden in light of the recent incident involving Maersk Hangzhou and ongoing developments in the area; all such vessels diverted south around the Cape of Good Hope

citation.title: Maersk Operations through Red Sea / Gulf of Aden (customer advisory hub, Maersk)
citation.quote: We have therefore decided that all Maersk vessels due to transit the Red Sea / Gulf of Aden will be diverted south around the Cape of Good Hope for the foreseeable future.
also: On 2nd January 2024, A.P. Moller – Maersk announced that it would pause all vessels bound for the Red Sea / Gulf of Aden in light of the recent incident involving Maersk Hangzhou and ongoing developments in the area.

also: On 15 December 2023 the container ship MSC PALATIUM III was attacked at approximately 09.37 UTC while transiting the Red Sea

entity_owed.reason: baseline_corridor_id equals reroute_corridor_id on every row because corridor identity (ORIGIN-DEST:mode, corridorSeed) cannot name the Suez or the Cape routing of one port pair. The producer does not mint an entity and does not weaken the distinct-corridor requirement: it writes the row on its existing key, counts the equality as a note on every run, and stops for the entity below.
